title: UDP or multicast source
description: MPEG-TS arriving over UDP, bare or in RTP, on a port or a multicast group.

address.title: Address
address.description: A multicast group to join, such as 239.1.1.1, or 0.0.0.0 to take whatever is sent to this machine's port.

port.title: Port
port.description: The UDP port the feed is sent to. Nothing listens on it until the source starts.

uri.title: Full address
uri.description: An address copied from VLC, ffmpeg or an IRD's settings, such as udp://@239.1.1.1:5000, rtp://@239.1.1.1:5004 or udp://10.0.0.9@232.1.1.1:5000. When set it wins over address and port. Bare MPEG-TS and RTP are told apart by themselves.

program.title: Program
program.description: Which program to take when the feed carries several, by number. 0 takes the first. The source's status lists the programs it finds, with their names and streams.

interface.title: Network interface
interface.description: The interface to join the multicast group on, by name: en0 or eth0 on macOS and Linux. Leave empty to use the one the default route goes through. Only needed on a machine with more than one network.

source_address.title: Only from sender
source_address.description: Source specific multicast: accept the group only from this sender's address. The group is usually in 232.0.0.0/8, and the network must support IGMPv3. Leave empty to accept any sender.

pids.title: Streams by PID
pids.description: Keep only these elementary streams, as PIDs separated by commas (256, 0x101). Useful to pick one audio language. Empty keeps every stream of the program. Naming PIDs without a program picks the program they belong to.

receive_buffer_kb.title: Receive buffer
receive_buffer_kb.description: How much the operating system may hold for this socket while the mixer is busy. 4 MB rides out a short pause at 30 Mbit/s. The system may cap it: on Linux raise net.core.rmem_max if the log says so.
